mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of tightening.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals a strengthening economy, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of increasing housing starts.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points in a single month signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and corporate costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of decreasing unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a single month signals increased economic activity and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of increasing industrial production.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than GDP (GDPC1) over a 3-month period, it signals a shift towards consumer-driven growth, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > GDPC1 growth over 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods where RSAFS growth exceeds GDPC1 growth.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over a single month signals a robust labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of simultaneous PAYEMS increase and UNRATE decrease.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in a single month signals inflationary pressures, which erodes real returns and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of increasing CPI.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 6-month decline in GDP (GDPC1) signals an economic slowdown, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of declining GDP.
